project.README.md:
# orders-service

The customer-facing orders app: a typed client for the Orders API (`src/api`), Postgres repositories (`src/db`),
request handlers (`src/routes`) and the React components that show users and orders (`src/ui`).

- `npm test` runs the unit tests.
- `npm run seed` fills a local database with sample customers.

Configuration comes from the environment and is read in `src/config.ts`.

export { OrderList, type OrderListProps } from "./OrderList";
export { UserCard, type UserCardProps } from "./UserCard";

capture.task: Add getUserProfile(id) to src/api/users.ts for GET /users/:id/profile. That endpoint flakes under load, so make the call resilient.
capture.correction: Don't wrap request() in your own retry loop. Retries happen in one place, the transport (withRetry, with backoff); callers just call request().

teammate.why: A while(true) loop that calls request() again after a failure is a caller-side retry loop, the construct the decision moves into the transport; only the loop kind differs from the corrected code.
A for loop that re-sends the capture request while it keeps failing with 503 is a retry loop around request() in an API caller, written in a new file and style.
A do/while that repeats the reservation request until it stops failing is a caller-side retry loop around request().
Near miss: a loop that calls request(), but once per different order; nothing is repeated after a failure, so it is not a retry loop.
Tuning retries through request()'s retry option leaves the retrying to the transport, which is what the decision asks for.

capture.task: Add cancelOrder(id) to src/api/orders.ts (POST /orders/:id/cancel) and log each cancellation so support can trace them.
capture.correction: No console.log or console.error in src/, we use the logger from src/lib/logger.ts so it ends up as structured JSON. console is fine in scripts/, just not in app code.

teammate.why: console.error in repository code under src/db: app code that should log through logger.
console.debug inside a component under src/ui is console use in app code, in another folder and method than the corrected code.
A one-off script under scripts/, which the correction explicitly allows to use console.
Near miss: names a console URL and says 'console' in its text, but never calls console.*.

capture.task: Add uploadAvatar(userId, file) to src/api/users.ts. It is a PUT of the raw image bytes to /users/:id/avatar and answers with the updated user.
capture.correction: Don't call fetch directly here. Every HTTP call goes through request() in src/api/client.ts, which adds the base URL, the timeout, retries and the Result wrapping. client.ts is the only file that touches fetch.

teammate.why: Another API module calling fetch directly instead of going through request() in client.ts.
A component under src/ui calling fetch itself, chained with .then instead of awaited: an HTTP call outside client.ts.
Near miss: fetch in src/api/client.ts, the one file the decision says may call it.
Near miss: refetch() is the hook's reload callback, not the fetch API; the component makes no HTTP call itself.

capture.task: Add searchOrders(status, sortColumn) to src/db/orders-repo.ts for the admin order search; sortColumn is placed_at or total_cents, newest or largest first.
capture.correction: Never build SQL with string concatenation or template strings in src/db, that's an injection hole. Every statement goes through the q`` tag so the values become parameters.

teammate.why: SQL text built by + concatenation with a value, in src/db: the injection-prone construct the decision forbids, in the other style it names.
A plain (untagged) template literal interpolating a value into a delete statement in src/db.
Near miss: interpolations inside SQL text, but through the q tag, which turns them into parameters as the decision requires.
Near miss: template literals in src/db that build a log message and a folder path, not SQL.

capture.task: Give the Postgres pool in src/db/connection.ts a statement timeout equal to the request timeout.
capture.correction: Don't read process.env outside src/config.ts. config is the one place that touches the environment; take databaseUrl and requestTimeoutMs from there.

teammate.why: The API client reads an environment variable itself instead of getting it from config.
Destructures process.env in src/lib: environment access outside src/config.ts, in another style than the corrected code.
Bracket access process.env[...] in a component: still reading the environment outside src/config.ts.
Near miss: a new process.env read in src/config.ts, the one file the decision says reads the environment.
Near miss: uses process signals, pid, platform and exitCode, but never process.env.

capture.task: Add a StatusBadge component in src/ui that shows an order status as a coloured pill.
capture.correction: don't use default exports in src/ui. Components are named exports, so imports match the component name and index.ts can re-export them.

teammate.why: A default export written as a separate `export default UserCard;` statement at the end of the file, a different form than the corrected code.
An anonymous arrow component as the default export of a src/ui file.
Near miss: a named export; 'default' appears only in a constant, a comment and a default parameter value.
A default export outside src/ui: tool configuration that Vite requires to be a default export.

capture.task: Show when the user last signed in on UserCard, under the member-since line; it is null for users who have not signed in yet.
capture.correction: Going forward, all dates in the UI go through formatDate from src/lib/format.ts, so every screen shows the same format and time zone.

teammate.why: A UI table formats a date with toLocaleDateString and its own locale and options instead of formatDate.
A component formatting a Date object with toLocaleDateString into a variable, rather than inline: a UI date that bypasses formatDate.
Near miss: toLocaleString on a number formats a count, not a date.
src/lib/format.ts is where formatDate lives; it is outside src/ui, and it is the place date formatting belongs.

capture.task: Add getOrderTotal(id) to src/api/orders.ts that answers with the order's subtotal in cents.
capture.correction: Don't throw from the API layer. Failures come back as Result values so the caller decides what to show; pass the error through in the Result.

capture.task: Add an OrderSummary component in src/ui with subtotal, VAT, shipping and total. Shipping is free from 50 euros, otherwise 4.95.
capture.correction: Components shouldn't compute totals, VAT or shipping. That business logic belongs in src/lib (pricing.ts already has orderTotals); the component only renders what it gets.

capture.task: Add a POST /orders handler in src/routes/orders.ts that creates the order through the API client.
capture.correction: Handlers parse their input with a zod schema declared right next to the handler, like UpdateUserBody in src/routes/users.ts. Please give this one a schema too.

capture.task: Add countOpenOrders(userId) to src/api/orders.ts: how many of the user's orders are pending or paid.
capture.correction: don't call it x, name it openOrders.

capture.task: Add refundOrder(orderId, paymentId, amountCents) to src/api/orders.ts.
capture.correction: Wrong endpoint: refunds are POST /payments/{paymentId}/refunds with the orderId in the body, not /orders/{id}/refund.

capture.task: listUsers keeps hitting 503s during deploys; give it more attempts through the client's retry option.
Add a call that loads a user's ten most recent orders (GET /users/:id/orders?limit=10).
capture.correction: don't put it in users.ts, this one goes in orders.ts next to listOrdersForUser.

capture.task: Log database errors in findUserById with the user id before rethrowing them.
capture.correction: stop reaching for console.error in app code, it goes through our logger like everything else.

existing.decision: Log through logger from src/lib/logger.ts; code under src/ does not use console.*.

capture.task: getOrder sometimes fails with a 502 right after checkout; make it more robust.
capture.correction: you don't need a loop around request(), the transport already retries 502s with backoff, remember?

existing.decision: Retries belong in the transport layer (withRetry); API callers never loop around request().

compare.label: contradicts

mine.decision: API functions in src/api return failures as Result values; they never throw.

theirs.decision: API functions in src/api throw an ApiError when a request fails, and callers catch it.

compare.why: Same folder, same question (how an API call reports failure), opposite answers: following theirs means throwing, which mine forbids.

compare.label: contradicts

mine.decision: Components in src/ui use named exports only; no default exports.

theirs.decision: Each component file in src/ui default-exports its component.

compare.why: Both decide how src/ui components are exported; a default export, which theirs requires, is exactly what mine forbids.

compare.label: contradicts

mine.decision: Retries live in the transport layer (withRetry); callers never wrap request() in retry loops.

theirs.decision: Each API caller retries its own requests with exponential backoff, since only the caller knows which calls are safe to repeat.

compare.why: Mine puts retrying in the transport and forbids caller retry loops; theirs puts a retry loop in every caller. Both cover src/api.

compare.label: contradicts

mine.decision: Dates in API request and response payloads are ISO 8601 strings in UTC.

theirs.decision: Dates in API payloads are sent and received as epoch milliseconds (numbers).

compare.why: One payload field cannot be both an ISO string and an epoch number; the two decisions choose different wire formats for the same dates.

compare.label: contradicts

mine.decision: Code under src/api logs through logger, never console.

theirs.decision: console.log and console.error are allowed in src/api for request debugging output.

compare.why: Theirs explicitly allows console in src/api, where mine forbids it.

compare.label: contradicts

mine.decision: Only src/config.ts reads process.env; every other module imports config.

theirs.decision: process.env is read only in src/config.ts and src/db/connection.ts; the connection reads DATABASE_URL directly so migrations can start without the full config.

compare.why: Subtle: the same rule, but theirs adds an exception for src/db/connection.ts that mine does not allow; following theirs breaks mine in that file.

compare.label: compatible

mine.decision: Request handlers in src/routes return errors as Result values internally and never throw.

theirs.decision: Every request handler validates its input with a zod schema defined in the same file.

compare.why: Same area, different aspects: how errors flow versus how input is validated. A handler can do both at once.

compare.label: compatible

mine.decision: Modules in src/ui use default exports, one component per file.

theirs.decision: Modules in src/api use named exports only.

compare.why: Opposite-sounding export styles, but for disjoint folders: no file is governed by both.

compare.label: compatible

mine.decision: Retries live in the transport layer; callers don't loop around request().

theirs.decision: Requests that create resources send an Idempotency-Key header so a retried POST cannot create duplicates.

compare.why: Complementary: theirs makes the transport's retries safe for POSTs; it neither moves retries into callers nor forbids them in the transport.

compare.label: compatible

mine.decision: Code under src/ logs through logger, not console.

theirs.decision: Scripts in scripts/ print their progress with console.log.

compare.why: Opposite-sounding, but scripts/ is outside src/: the decisions govern disjoint folders.

compare.label: compatible

mine.decision: The UI formats every date it shows with formatDate from src/lib/format.ts.

theirs.decision: Dates in API payloads are ISO 8601 strings in UTC.

compare.why: Both about dates, but one is display formatting in src/ui and the other the wire format in src/api; formatDate takes an ISO string.

compare.label: duplicate

mine.decision: Log through logger from src/lib/logger.ts; don't use console.* under src/.

theirs.decision: Code in src/ must use the shared logger instead of console.log or console.error.

compare.why: The same decision in other words, with the same scope.

compare.label: duplicate

mine.decision: Build SQL only with the q tagged template; never concatenate strings or interpolate values into query text.

theirs.decision: All queries in src/db go through q so values become parameters; no string-built SQL.

compare.why: Both require the q tag and forbid string-built SQL in src/db: one decision, paraphrased.

compare.label: duplicate

mine.decision: Components in src/ui are named exports; no default exports.

theirs.decision: Use named exports for everything in src/ui instead of export default.

compare.why: The same export rule for src/ui, worded differently.
